document.title: IIR [Excised]/The Assassination of Massoud Related to 11 September 2001 Attack
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Taliban File
document.note: [Secret] DIA assesses the link between the assassination of Northern Alliance Commander Ahmad Shah Masoud and the 9/11 attacks. Masoud had apparently gained limited knowledge of Bin Ladin's and al-Qaida's intentions to attack the US on a scale larger than the 1998 embassy bombings.

persons.status_detail: Assassinated in northern Afghanistan by a suicide bomb; the report states 9 September 2001 in the background and 2 September 2001 in the relationships paragraph (likely an OCR error)

organizations.name: Northern Alliance
organizations.notes: Formed by Massoud to continue the fight against the Taliban in northern Afghanistan; its intelligence reports gave Massoud limited knowledge of al-Qa'ida's intentions.

organizations.name: Taliban
organizations.notes: Began in the early 1990s as religious students rejecting the mujahidin takeover; Pakistani government support made them militarily powerful, controlling about 30 percent of Afghanistan (the figure is as printed, likely an OCR error).

organizations.name: al-Qa'ida
organizations.notes: Usama bin Ladin's organization; its members posed as journalists to assassinate Massoud. The report links this to the 11 September 2001 attacks.

events.description: Bombings of US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania; the report treats them as the benchmark for the larger attack Massoud had warned about.
Massoud addressed the French and European Parliaments in Paris, and in a televised speech warned the US government about UBL.

Massoud was assassinated in northern Afghanistan by two al-Qa'ida-linked Arabs posing as journalists, using a suicide bomb. The relationships paragraph gives the date as 2 September (likely an OCR error).

DIA issued this IIR on the relationship between the Massoud assassination and 9/11.

key_claims: The DIA report links al-Qa'ida's assassination of Massoud to the 11 September 2001 attacks.
Two Arabs loyal to UBL and belonging to al-Qa'ida posed as journalists and killed Massoud with a suicide bomb.
Through Northern Alliance intelligence reports Massoud gained limited knowledge of an al-Qa'ida plan for an attack on the US larger than the 1998 embassy bombings.
Massoud warned the French and European Parliaments and the US government about UBL in April 2001.
Massoud was not a direct threat to UBL; the report presents UBL as a Saudi exile in Afghanistan.
Pakistani government support made the Taliban militarily powerful against outgunned Afghan opposition forces.
